relevance_note: Case report of a man with Tangier disease and a homozygous ABCA1 variant: "a likely pathogenic variant in the ABCA1 gene was identified by whole-exome sequencing (WES), identified for the first time as homozygous".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; values were typed into a small Python builder script that asserts every span is found verbatim in the paper. No tables in the paper (Tables S1/S2 are not included in the Markdown). Scope: index patient ('patient'); three brothers who died of premature cardiovascular death and are described with features (neuropathy, low ApoA-I/ApoB, thrombocytopenia, splenomegaly) but were never genetically tested (authors: could be affected by TD, 'cannot be confirmed due to the lack of genetic testing'); the fifth (living) sibling carrying 'the same variants in homozygous state'; and the previously published Fasano et al. [38] patient (compound heterozygous for c.4799A>G; second allele not printed, so one variant row). Left out: the parents ('both died at an elderly age', untested, no features) and the sibling who 'died of laryngeal cancer' (untested, no TD features). The three brothers are described only together, so labels 'brother of patient', '... 2', '... 3' are arbitrary in order; the brother who had emergency splenectomy for spontaneous splenic rupture ('one of them') was assigned to 'brother of patient'. Their group features are recorded as 'inferred from group statement' for each brother. The living sibling's variant row copies c.4799A>G / p. His1600Arg / NM_005502.4 from the index patient's description because the paper says 'the same variants in homozygous state' (plural 'variants' in the paper); both spans are given. Pathogenicity/ACMG were not carried over to the sibling. Patient's peripheral neuropathy left 'not reported' on the checklist: sural sensory amplitude asymmetry 'cannot be definitely linked to neuropathic manifestation of Tangier disease since he also suffers from lumbar degenerative disc disease'. Slit-lamp 'crystalline powdery opacities affecting both eyes' recorded as a feature, but the checklist item 'corneal opacity' left 'not reported' because the paper does not say the opacities are corneal. Absence of corneal arcus does not exclude corneal opacity (narrow vs broad). Absence of foamy histiocytes was in gastric antral biopsies, so 'intestinal mucosal lipid deposits' left 'not reported'. Unremarkable chest X-ray, ECG, ABPM, stress echocardiogram and urine albumin/creatinine ratio recorded as excluded abnormal results of each test as the paper names them (D-27); they exclude nothing more specific, so coronary artery disease is 'not reported'. Possible tension (not a contradiction): mild blood pressure elevation on examination vs unremarkable ambulatory blood pressure monitoring; both recorded. Discussion phrases 'family history of coronary heart disease' about the siblings were not used to mark CAD, since the text describes 'premature cardiovascular death'/'unexpected sudden death' without naming CAD per brother. n_patients_reported = 1 from 'we describe a case study of a 59-year-old male patient'; the paper also describes the homozygous sibling and the Fasano [38] patient. In silico predictions and SWISS-MODEL protein modelling are not functional assays, so functional_evidence_statement is 'not reported'. Age 59 is the age at referral/report (recorded as last evaluation); no age at onset or diagnosis is given. Chest trauma history at 21 (pneumothorax, T11 burst fracture), smoking and sedentary lifestyle were not recorded as phenotypic features.
